newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria set to win $290 mln in World Bank loans.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria set to win $290 mln in World Bank loans.

text.p: The World Bank is prepared to extend $290 million to Bulgaria if the government speeds up privatisation of state factories and banks and eliminates public sector losses, a World Bank official said on Friday.

"The goal is to recover growth, bring down inflation, have a private sector that would expand employment and exports," visiting World Bank chief economist for Europe and Central Asia, Marcelo Selowsky told a news conference.

The World Bank and the interim cabinet have agreed on a reform and funding programme consisting of three loans linked to agreements to be reached with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), said Selowksky.
The first $40 million loan would be for imports of essential goods like grain, fuel and medical supplies, which will be offered to the World Bank board for approval in April, said Selowsky.

The second is a social safety net loan of $80 million to be targeted to the most vulnerable social groups like pensioners, jobless and the disabled. The loan will be offered to the board for approval in June.
The third credit, for financial reform and restructuring enterprises, consists of two loans totalling around $170 million. The first disbursement is expected in June and the second in December.
Liberalisation of prices to increase farm supplies from local producers to offset current shortages is also part of the reform targets, said Selowsky.

The caretaker cabinet appointed four weeks ago has pledged to speed up privatisation, shut down loss-making state companies and liberalise prices and trade rules. It will remain in office until after general elections on April 19.

Next week, the interim cabinet hopes to reach a preliminary agreement with the IMF for the implementation of a fixed exchange rate mechanism to help stabilise the economy. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
